Judge at the gate a revocation somebody other than its creator made

scope_withdrawal.Rd

The second half of the exception change_needs_approval() makes for a revocation, the half only an instance can answer. The round holds the row provisionally until it knows who manages the project, and this is where it finds out.

Usage

scope_withdrawal(row, authors, creator, sealed, rights)

Arguments

row

The row, one line of the register as the gate reads it.

authors

Who has a hand in the change, as log_pending_authors() answers.

creator

Who created the row.

sealed

Whether the row carries the seal of an execution.

rights

The rights the instance reported, as round_rights() builds them.

Value

"" when the revocation stands; "held" when it waits for the creator; otherwise the refusal code, as scope_errors() gives it.

Details

The question is the gate's own, asked of different people. A revocation stands on the authority of whoever had a hand in it, so each of them is asked "could you have done this by hand", which for a removal is "do you hold User Rights on this project". The creator is asked only when the creator is one of them: a creator who no longer manages the project does not stop a manager from removing somebody, since the manager could have done it in REDCap anyway.

Three answers. A permission that could not be read is ours, as on the ordinary gate, and keeps the row queued. A creator who had a hand in it and does not manage the project is refused as the creator's own change would be. Anybody else who does not manage it puts the row back under the common rule: it waits for the creator.
